answers.answer: Use the table under Every built-in command to find the command that does your task. To change its reply, go to Commands, open the System commands tab and click the command's row in the Built-in commands list. If the fields are locked, choose Customize in the footer. Edit the reply box, then choose Save changes.
answers.quote: If the fields are locked, choose Customize in the footer first.

answers.answer: You need a role that shows the System commands tab. By default that is a moderator, a lead moderator, an editor or the broadcaster. It is stated at the top of the page and again at the start of Change a built-in command. A data-rights command cannot be changed at all.
answers.quote: You need the role that shows the System commands tab: by default a moderator or higher.

answers.answer: After Save changes, the count of unsaved changes leaves the footer and a Back to default button shows under each field you changed. That button means the bot now uses your wording. In the list, a row that says Overrides the default (…) has a changed role or cooldown. A row that says Using the default has not.
answers.quote: That button shows only for a saved change, so it tells you the bot uses your wording from now on.

answers.answer: The moderator should edit the built-in command in its editor and not make a channel command with the same name. A channel command with the same name answers in place of the built-in one, so the original is hidden, not changed. The exceptions are !permit, !unpermit and the data-rights commands. If a copy already exists, delete it so the built-in command answers again. Data-rights replies cannot be changed.
answers.quote: So a copy hides the original rather than changing it.

answers.answer: Three things are learned only after the action they affect. A command that another item still runs cannot be switched off: the switch flips back and an Action required item appears. The page does not say where the Action required inbox is. For !permit and !unpermit, a moderator learns only lower down that Moderators in Who can use it does not let them give permits. On a shared command, a reset also resets the shared replies of the other command, which is said before the reset steps but after the lurk and stats editing steps. Each one costs a reread or a failed attempt.
answers.quote: The switch then goes back on, and the Action required inbox shows “Not saved: Turn off built-in command” with the command’s name.

answers.answer: Read aloud, the table of 43 commands with two cooldown columns is long, and most cells are 0 s. A listener looking for one command must sit through all of them. The note that the editor says Only you while the list row says Broadcaster also takes a second listen to keep straight.
answers.quote: The editor names this role Only you, and the row in the Built-in commands list says Broadcaster.
